5.3 Decoding the Metrics of Student Engagement and 
Performance with Empirical Insights 
The following metrics were derived and fabricated from the frameworks by 
(Brame, 2016; de Jong, 2009) and insights from (Twenge & Campbell, 2018) for 
their potential influence on the learning outcome and students’ attention span.  
Given that attention spans have likely reduced due to increased screen time 
(Twenge & Campbell, 2018; Gausby, 2015) this study will measure the 
engagement, attention spans and distractibility levels as key features. 
Engagement is quantified through observation of the student or duration of 
sessions and the applications usage frequency. Distractibility will be defined by 
how easily a student’s attention is drawn to external stimuli such as notifications 
or shutting doors; again, this could be measured by observation or how 
frequently the user exits the app. 
Of course, the primary objective of any e-learning platform is to educate its 
students. Perceived learning for this study will be defined as the quantity of 
information retained and the degree of content mastery. This can be measured 
in two ways, firstly, the researcher could ask the student how much they believe 
they have learned, or second, examine the student at the end of the lesson. 
Considering the critical role that usability has in e-learning, and the limited 
research surrounding it (Lee, 2021). A metric to measure the applications design 
and user interface to ensure it does not inadvertently increase extraneous load, 
is critical to ensure an optimal learning experience. This can be measured 
through observation and qualitative feedback.
